title: Unbounded module evaluation of component pullback on w-contractible tests
statement:
Let $W$ be a w-contractible affine scheme [sk-def-pe-wlocal], let $S=\pi_0(W)$ with its profinite quotient topology, and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Use the small pro-etale site and compatible coefficient universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Give $\operatorname{Prof}/S$ finite jointly surjective coverings, let $q_S$ be its slice projection to the condensed topos, put $\Lambda_S=q_S^*\Lambda$, and let $\pi_W$ be the component morphism with $p_W=q_S\pi_W$ [lem-zl-component-relative-profinite-site]. Write $F_W=\pi_W^*$ on module sheaves and on their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with coefficient identification $F_W\Lambda_S=p_W^*\Lambda$. For every w-contractible affine object $U\to W$, put $T=\pi_0(U)$, with its induced map to $S$. For every $\Lambda_S$-module sheaf $M$ there is a canonical identification
$$(F_WM)(U)=M(T\to S),$$
natural in $M$ and in maps between such $U$, and linear for the canonical identification $(p_W^*\Lambda)(U)=\Lambda(T)$. Evaluation at $U$ on module sheaves over $W$ and evaluation at $T$ on module sheaves over $\operatorname{Prof}/S$ are exact. For every unbounded $K\in D(\operatorname{Prof}/S,\Lambda_S)$ there is a natural isomorphism of entire derived objects
$$R\Gamma(T,K|_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(U,F_WK),$$
where restriction means restriction to $\operatorname{Prof}/T$, and derived sections are computed termwise by these exact evaluations [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. Its normalization is the degreewise displayed module identification, in the pullback direction. In particular at $U=W$ it is the canonical pullback of global sections. Empty $W,U$ and arbitrary unbounded complexes are allowed.

proof.text: Apply the proved source isWeaklyContractible_of_iso to the affine test U with its canonical isoSpec. A finite qcqs cover gives a locally surjective map of representable set sheaves from the coproduct to U. Projectivity lifts the identity section, providing a section of that coproduct map. Hence U has the split-cover property required by affine_component_site_projection.

The relative component-test universal mapping property constructs the canonical lift U to the test indexed by pi_0(U). It also proves that every compatible b,c factors through this lift and that the lifts are natural in U. Define the abelian section comparison by the fixed sheaf-pullback adjunction unit followed by restriction along the lift. Its normalization and naturality follow directly from this factorization and naturality of the unit.

Use relative_component_lift_pullback_space to identify the relative-test and affine-test functors. Transport their pushforwards and adjunctions through this isomorphism. Uniqueness of left adjoints and the normalized evaluation clause of affine_component_site_projection show that the section comparison composed with the known evaluation isomorphism is the identity. It is therefore invertible.

Use the canonical strong braided structure and exactness of component inverse image. Its monoidal adjunction unit, the restriction comparison, and evaluation are monoidal, so the section comparison preserves tensor actions and coefficient multiplication. Convert the resulting internal commutative rings and module objects to the actual section rings and section modules. The alpha,beta coefficient factorization is the corresponding clause of condensed_component_pullback_compatibility. Restriction along alpha inverse cancels alpha in the section-ring comparison, giving linearity.

Evaluation at U preserves finite limits. Weak contractibility turns locally surjective maps of set sheaves into surjective maps on sections, so evaluation of abelian sheaves preserves epimorphisms and is exact. Forgetting the module action preserves finite limits and colimits and reflects them, yielding exact target module evaluation. The section comparison then transports exactness of pullback followed by target evaluation and scalar restriction to source evaluation. Apply the existing exact-functor right-derived unit theorem and the already defined componentEvaluationDerivedIso to obtain the ordinary unbounded comparison.
